tb21_profile.skill: Infer a probabilistic model's structure from observational data (dependence/correlation plus an orientation rule), fit its parameters, mutilate it with a do-intervention, and resample from the modified generative model
tb21_profile.domain: Probabilistic graphical models / causal inference over tabular continuous data; statistics stack (R bnlearn or Python pgmpy/pandas/numpy)
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec data-analysis pipeline emitting exactly formatted CSV artifacts (edge lists plus a resampled dataset)

notes: No corpus contains a causal-inference or Bayesian-network structure-learning task; searches for bnlearn, pgmpy, conditional independence, partial correlation and do-calculus all returned nothing. The retrieval shortlist for this task is badly poisoned: 'DAG' in these corpora almost always means a build/task dependency graph (Makefile, Airflow, pipdeptree), and the TMax shortlist was dominated by CSV edge-list graph-analytics chores that share the word 'graph' and nothing else. I discarded those and rebuilt the pools around the two real sub-skills: (a) fit a joint/generative model to a table and sample from it, and (b) infer structure from a numeric data matrix. TMax carries (a) well; SWE-Rebench contributes the SDV/copulas and pymc/numpyro probabilistic-modelling libraries, which are the best domain matches anywhere in the pool. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis have nothing closer than generic sklearn pipelines and exact-format CSV chores, and are scored accordingly.
